newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty International plans first billboard drive.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty International plans first billboard drive.

text.p: Amnesty International, the human rights charity, said on Friday that it was launching its first billboard advertising campaign, aimed at raising awareness about the group among Britons under 30.

Three different billboard formats featuring black-and-white news photos of real victims of abuse, torture and murder were being put up throughout Britain from Sunday and would remain for two weeks, it said.

The three billboards carry the headlines, "Abused by Security Forces. Exposed by Amnesty International"; "Tortured by the State. Exposed by Amnesty International"; and "Murdered by Death Squads. Exposed by Amnesty International."
Each billboard also carries the tagline, "The Human Right Thing to Do."
"A good proportion of people feel human rights is such a massive problem you can't do anything. But you can," said Norma Johnston, a spokeswoman for Amnesty International.

"We're trying to reach under 30s," Johnston said. "A lot of research suggest they're more likely to read posters than newspapers." The 320 billboard sites in the campaign are in cities throughout Britain, with a strong orientation toward main shopping street sites likely to be seen by those under 30.
"People over 30 have grown up with Amnesty International", Johnston said. "They know it. But younger people don't."
"This is not a fund-raising thing," she added. "It is to raise awareness."

Johnston said the billboard campaign is Amnesty International's most expensive advertising campaign ever, although she declined to detail the amount. The billboards were designed by the Michael Peters Partnership.
